summary: Charles DiSimone works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a post at the University of Munich (attested 2021) and serves as co-director and permanent member at Ghent University (attested 2026).

Charles Duroiselle (1871–1951) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He taught Pali at the University of Yangon (~1906–1919) and served as Superintendent of the Archaeological Survey of Burma (1912–1940).

Charles Edmund Godakumbura (1907–1977), an Indologist and archaeologist, earned multiple degrees at the University of London, where he later taught (~1953–1959). He served as Sri Lanka's Commissioner of Archaeology (1956–1967) and President of the Royal Asiatic Society of Sri Lanka (~1963–1970).

Charles Eliot (1862–1931) worked in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. After studying at Balliol College, Oxford, he worked for the Foreign Office (~1886–1926) and served at the University of Sheffield (~1905–1912) and as principal of the University of Hong Kong (~1912–1918).

Charles Elliott (1776–1856) was an Indologist. He served in the East India Company (~1795–1819) and later held the post of Treasurer at the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland (~1837–1856).

Charles Gabriel Seligman (1873–1940) studied medicine at St Thomas's Hospital Medical School (~1892–1896). He held the chair of ethnology at the London School of Economics and Political Science and the University of London from 1913 to 1934.

Charles Goodman specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Michigan under Allan Gibbard in 2002 and served as an associate professor at Binghamton University (attested 2013).

Charles H. Long (1926–2020) was a religious studies scholar educated at Dunbar Junior College and the University of Chicago (PhD 1962). He held posts at Chicago (~1956–1974), UNC Chapel Hill, Duke (~1974–1987), Syracuse (~1987–1991), and UC Santa Barbara (~1991–1996).

Charles Hallisey (b. 1953) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar educated at Colgate, Harvard, UPenn, and the University of Chicago. He held faculty posts at Loyola University Chicago, Harvard University, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

Charles Henry Tawney (1837–1922) was an Indologist educated at Trinity College, Cambridge. He taught at Trinity College, led Presidency College in Kolkata (1875–1892), and served as Librarian of the India Office (1892/1893–1903).

Charles Li works in Indology, philosophy, and computational fields. He held a postdoctoral fellowship at the University of British Columbia (attested 2020) and a project research post at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

Charles Malamoud (b. 1929) is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who was educated at the University of Paris. He taught at the University of Lyon (~1960–1972) and was Directeur d'Études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1979–1998).
Charles Oman (1860–1946) was a historian and archaeologist. He studied at New College, Oxford (~1878–1882) and held an academic post at the University of Oxford from around 1883 to 1946.

Charles Otto Blagden (1864–1949) was a scholar of linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at Corpus Christi College, Oxford, under William Robertson, and held a post at SOAS University of London from ~1917 to 1935.

Charles Philip Brown (1798–1884), an Indologist and linguist, studied at East India Company College and under traditional teachers in India. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1817–1854) and was Professor of Telugu at the University of London (~1855–1879).

Charles Ramble (b. 1957) is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies educated at Durham University under Michael Aris. He has held professorships at the University of Oxford (2002–2005) and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (from 2009).

Charles Rieu (1820–1902) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. Educated at Geneva and Bonn under Lassen, Humbert, Freytag, and Gildemeister, he served as Curator of Oriental Manuscripts at the British Museum and Adams Professor of Arabic at Cambridge.

Charles Rockwell Lanman (1850–1941) was an Indologist and linguist. Educated at Yale and in Germany under Whitney, Weber, Roth, Curtius, and Leskien, he taught at Johns Hopkins (1876–1880) and served as professor at Harvard University (1880–1926).

Charles S. Prebish (b. 1944) is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar educated at Case Western Reserve University and taught by David M. Miller and Richard Hugh Robinson. He was a longtime professor at Pennsylvania State University (~1972–2007).

Charles Taliaferro (b. 1952) is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. Educated at Goddard College, the University of Rhode Island, Harvard Divinity School, and Brown University, he served as a professor at St. Olaf College from ~1985 to 2022.
